claims.text: The article describes a setup that is running, as the agents who run it wrote it down on 6 October 2026, with the reasons and the earlier arguments added back so it can be copied.
claims.quote: as the agents who run it wrote it down on 6 October 2026

claims.text: On 6 October 2026 the team had twelve agents, four scheduled runs a day on weekdays, 71 people in the CRM, and zero emails sent by an agent on its own, the row the design is organised around.
claims.quote: That last row is the one the whole design is organised around.

value.unit: emails an agent sent on its own

claims.text: Twelve agents, each a Claude session on a dedicated account with a written brief and an Agent Behaviour Policy read before work; eleven of the twelve policies forbid sending.
claims.quote: Eleven of the twelve policies forbid the same thing: sending.

claims.text: The only memory is encrypted vaults driven by sgit: files are encrypted on the agent's side before they leave, the host stores ciphertext, and keys are handed to each session out of band and never written into a file.
claims.quote: Files are encrypted on the agent's side before they leave; the host stores ciphertext and never holds a key.

claims.text: Nothing the agents use belongs to the person: a dedicated Google Workspace, a dedicated Claude Team account, encrypted vaults, and a separate personal agent on the person's own domain.
claims.quote: Nothing the agents use belongs to the person.

claims.text: The account boundary is the first control because it is the one that does not depend on anyone behaving; a policy asks an agent not to look, a boundary means there is nothing to see.
claims.quote: This is the first control because it is the one that does not depend on anyone behaving.

claims.text: The roles are split so each policy is short enough to check, and they differ where it matters: one role reads the mailbox, one writes drafts into it, and none sends from it.
claims.quote: One role reads it, one role writes drafts into it, and none sends from it.

claims.text: Agents do not call each other; they write .eml files into each other's mailroom folder in the shared vault, a convention the team calls Email-FS lite, and the recipient moves, acts and files.
claims.quote: Agents do not call each other.

claims.text: The conductor runs the team four times a day on weekdays, security first and last, each agent one step of up to twelve minutes; nothing loops, and a run that dies leaves a lock the next run notices.
claims.quote: A run that dies leaves a lock, and the next run notices and says so.

claims.text: Always commit before pulling: the team reports that a pull overwrites uncommitted edits in the local working tree, which two agents learned by losing work; it is reported here rather than yet filed against the CLI.
claims.quote: which two agents learned by losing work

claims.text: Each session ends with a card: a script reads the transcript afterwards, counts tools, tokens, files and network calls, and flags anything outside the agent's policy; the card is the footprint measured from the record.
claims.quote: The card is the footprint, measured after the fact from the record

claims.text: The first card flagged two writes as outside the mandate; on inspection the policy allowed them and the script had misread it, and both findings are in the record.
claims.quote: on inspection the policy allowed them and the script had misread it

claims.text: The CRM is a vault of plain JSON and Markdown with no database: one folder per person, an append-only ledger, every message with provenance and a hash, a graph of interests, and a generated summary never hand-edited.
claims.quote: There is no database. Each person gets a folder

claims.text: Inbound is data: nothing stored is ever acted on as an instruction, and a message from the world is a fact about the world, not a command to the team.
claims.quote: A message from the world is a fact about the world, not a command to the team.

claims.text: A what we know about you pack can be sent to the person to correct, and a memory that can be shown to its subject is one kept to what can be shown.
claims.quote: a memory that can be shown to its subject is a memory that has been kept to what can be shown

claims.text: Four rules are never negotiated: keys never go into any file, no agent sends except @security's one hold email, no agent changes a scheduled task, and create anywhere, edit your own.
claims.quote: Agents create drafts; a person sends.

claims.text: The rule that only one agent may draft became a bottleneck in two days and was replaced by create anywhere, edit your own, keeping the property that no agent rewrites another's work.
claims.quote: became a bottleneck in two days

claims.text: The team grades its barriers: identity and encryption strong, grant medium, record medium, policy weak; many rows, including no agent sends, rely on the policy text.
claims.quote: most of this team's barriers are weaker than anyone would like

claims.text: RiskMandate's vocabulary types a barrier as boundary, setting, expectation or none, and only a boundary is a control; identity and encryption are boundaries, the record and the policy are expectations.
claims.quote: a control bounds a grant only if it is enforced by something the grant does not include

claims.text: A connector appeared mid-session giving reach to thousands of apps through Zapier, and three agents flagged it as outside their policy before using it.
claims.quote: Three agents flagged it as outside their policy before using it.

claims.text: Calendar invites have no draft state, so a person sends cannot be written for calendars, and whoever grants the calendar accepts that risk, which the policy now says.
claims.quote: Calendar invites have no draft state.

claims.text: A discarded Gmail draft is gone with no log, and Gmail drafts strip images; the workaround of sending pictures through Zapier, a 9,000-app reach to send one picture, was refused.
claims.quote: a 9,000-app reach to send one picture

value.unit: apps reachable through the refused workaround

claims.text: The host cannot read the memory: every file, filename, commit message and branch name is encrypted with AES-256-GCM and per-file keys from HKDF-SHA256, rooted in a vault key that never travels to the server.
claims.quote: the key hierarchy rooted in a vault key that never travels to the server

claims.text: A read key is derived one way and cannot write, an append lane is a write-only token, and a leaked write key means a new vault because history holds what redaction removes.
claims.quote: History holds what redaction removes

claims.text: The team can be stopped by a hold file: while it is open the conductor refuses to open a run and every step refuses to start, and only a person releases it.
claims.quote: Only a person releases it.

claims.text: Three platform limits apply: commit authorship is not yet signed, there is no key revocation, and the lane that would let two vaults message without a person is not wired end to end.
claims.quote: commit authorship is not yet signed

claims.text: Information is handled in three classes, public, private-ish and personal, and the class decides where it may live; the team's vaults hold the first two and refuse the third.
claims.quote: Information is handled in three classes, and the class decides where it may live.

claims.text: Personal information is not captured even when it arrives in a message, credentials are never stored, and the recipient's privacy outranks the team's completeness.
claims.quote: the recipient's privacy outranks the team's completeness

claims.text: Because the policy is a file per agent and the memory a folder per person, rules can be scoped to one customer and written to protect the recipient; a tighter rule is a line in a file.
claims.quote: A customer who asks for a tighter rule gets a line in a file, not a product roadmap.

claims.text: The setup is files not a database, graphs inside graphs, and Claude as a state machine: each role reads its state from files, does one kind of work, writes it back and stops.
claims.quote: It does not converse; it runs a step.

claims.text: Two registers disagree on how many emails have been sent, so the dashboards under-count until they are reconciled.
claims.quote: so the dashboards under-count until the registers are reconciled

claims.text: Messaging between vaults still needs a person to paste text, because the encrypted lane between them needs re-keying.
claims.quote: Messaging between vaults still needs a person

claims.text: There is no daily brief channel to the person: WhatsApp got the account suspended in testing and Discord failed twice.
claims.quote: WhatsApp got the account suspended in testing, and Discord failed twice.

claims.text: Most barriers are policy-only: the platform does not let the team remove send tools per agent, and the separate permission authority that would make no agent sends a block does not exist yet.
claims.quote: The platform does not let the team remove send tools per agent

claims.text: Who gives the mandate over a piece of information, and whether the recipient of an email has the authority to hand it to an agent at all, is left open and gets a document of its own.
claims.quote: who gives the mandate over a piece of information, and whether the recipient of an email has the authority to hand it to an agent at all
